narrative: Material PL1__M560A5BF exhibits regular demand with moderate variability (CV=0.488). Analysis of 140 working days reveals a mean daily demand of 414.84 units with 97.9% non-zero demand days and a statistically significant upward trend. Lead time analysis from 41 observations confirms moderate stability (CV=0.382, mean 4.15 days). The optimised (r,Q) continuous-review policy recommends safety stock of 1,267 units and order quantity of 7,064 units (capacity-constrained from EOQ of 8,266), yielding annual savings of $2,889.16 (64.4% reduction). Storage capacity is critically tight at 99.9% utilisation post-replenishment.
warnings: Storage capacity is critically tight: safety_stock + order_quantity = 8331 units = 99.9% of max_storage_units (8331.372)
EOQ (8266) was capped to 7064 due to storage capacity constraint (max_storage_units - safety_stock = 7064)
Upward demand trend detected (statistically significant) - policy should be reviewed periodically

research_insights.selection_rationale: With 97.9% non-zero demand days and regular demand pattern (CV=0.488), a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is optimal. The material has sufficiently high and consistent demand to justify EOQ-based lot sizing. A fixed MOQ of 2,312 units exists but the EOQ (8,266) dominates, making batch ordering efficient. Continuous review is preferred over periodic review given moderate lead time variability that could cause stockouts during fixed review intervals.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity constraint is binding: the unconstrained EOQ of 8,266 units was reduced to 7,064 units to satisfy max_storage_units=8,331.372 with safety_stock=1,267. Post-replenishment inventory fills 99.9% of warehouse capacity, leaving virtually no buffer for demand surges or early deliveries. This constraint increases annual ordering frequency slightly above the unconstrained optimum and elevates stockout risk during peak demand periods. Warehouse capacity expansion or demand-based dynamic ordering should be considered.
